newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - BRUINS BEAT FLYERS TO END SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - BRUINS BEAT FLYERS TO END SLIDE.

text.p: Bill Ranford made 34 saves and Adam Oates and Kyle McLaren scored second-period goals as the Boston Bruins stopped a three-game winless streak with a 2-0 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers on Tuesday.
Ranford made 14 saves in the first period, 11 in the second and nine in the third for his second career shutout against Philadelphia.
Eric Lindros, the 1995 Hart Trophy winner, made his season debut for the Flyers, after missing 23 games with a groin injury.

At Florida, Ray Sheppard recorded his ninth career hat trick and Robert Svehla scored in the third period as the Florida Panthers overcame a two-goal deficit for their fourth straight victory, 4-3 over the Buffalo Sabres.

"Everything I threw at the net went in," Sheppard said. "I got a breakaway, the defenceman got on me and I did a spin-o-rama and it went in. A move like that doesn't always work, if it doesn't, people say he's some sort of clown."

In Calgary, Todd Marchant, Mats Lindgren, Doug Weight and Miroslav Satan each had a goal and an assist and Curtis Joseph came within 4:09 of a shutout as the Edmonton Oilers routed the Calagry Flames, 10-1 for their third straight win.
The Flames, which suffered their worst loss in Saddledome history, are 2-9-1 in their last 12 games.
With the Oilers leading 2-0 in the second, rookie Mats Lindgren slammed a rebound of Rem Murray's shot past Trevor Kidd for his second goal at 1:55 of the second.
Edmonton made it 4-0 less than three minutes later past Kidd, who was lifted in the second period after allowing four goals on just 10 shots.

In Toronto, Marcel Cousineau made 22 saves for his first NHL win and Wendel Clark, Darby Hendrickson and Mats Sundin all scored first-period goals as the Toronto Maple Leafs defeated the Vancouver Canucks 3-2.
The win was just Toronto's second in its last eight games.
Cousineau became the backup goaltender when Toronto waived Don Beaupre earlier this month.
In Phoenix, Mark Messier recorded his first hat trick of the season and Mike Richter stopped 37 shots to lead the New York Rangers to a 3-1 victory over the slumping Phoenix Coyotes.
Messier scored two first-period goals, and with the Rangers nursing a 2-1 lead in the final minute, added an empty-net tally with 14 seconds to play for his 18th career hat trick.
The three goals moved Messier past Michel Goulet and into 13th place on the all-time list with 551, five behind Johnny Bucyk.
